title: BBQ Sauce
summary: American condiment family — sweet Kansas City to vinegar Carolina to pepper Texas.
origins: American barbecue sauce evolved regionally from British colonists' vinegar-and-pepper basting liquids, German immigrant mustard traditions in the Carolinas, and Kansas City meatpackers' sweet tomato-based glazes in the early 1900s. There is no single original recipe — geography defines the bottle.
history: Commercial bottled sauce took off after WWII when suburban grills met supermarket convenience. Heinz and Kraft popularized thick tomato-molasses styles; regional pitmasters kept vinegar-pepper and white Alabama sauces alive. Today most pantry bottles lean Kansas City sweet — great on bowls, not historically what Texas brisket pits use at the table.
teaching: Most bottles are Kansas City sweet — balance with acid (lime, vinegar) in bowls.
Add sauce last on high heat — sugars burn above ~325°F.
Thin with stock or bean liquid instead of water for deeper flavor.
fun_fact: Most BBQ sauces are Kansas City sweet, Carolina vinegar, or Texas bold — this meal leans bowl, not pit.
